chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"When a man has intercourse with his wife from behind (in the anus) while she is fasting, her fast is not broken, and there is no ghusl (ritual bath) upon her."
Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: This report is not acted upon, and its chain of narration is disconnected (maqtu'), so it is not relied upon.

key_terms.لَا يُعَوَّلُ عَلَيْهِ: not relied upon / not acted upon

ai.seo_question: Does anal intercourse break the wife's fast and require ghusl?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights a specific juristic view that anal intercourse does not invalidate the wife’s fast nor require *ghusl*, distinguishing it from vaginal intercourse. However, Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Mar’ashi notes its practical unreliability due to a disconnected chain (*maqtu’ al-isnad*), reflecting the critical scrutiny applied to *Tahdhib* reports in Shia fiqh. This underscores the distinction between a report’s textual validity and its operational authority in legal derivation.
